_comment: The Object Lifecycle Management rules for `stockbook-content-{env}`.
Applied by scripts/ops/setup-gcs-lifecycle.sh, which MERGES them into
whatever policy the bucket already carries.
RENAMED from `gcs-lifecycle-edgar.json` by MONEY-1309. The old name was
accurate for two releases and stopped being so the moment a second prefix
moved in: a policy file whose NAME asserts a scope its CONTENTS violate is
the same defect the guard below exists to catch, one layer up.
## Read this before adding a rule
A lifecycle policy is set on a BUCKET, not on a prefix, and
`gcloud storage buckets update --lifecycle-file` REPLACES the whole policy.
`stockbook-content-{env}` also holds `feeds/` (the prod->QA exchange-feed
mirror, 66,951 objects at the 2026-08-13 parity check), `candles/` (every
cold price shard), learning content, user documents and the RAG corpus. A
rule here with no `matchesPrefix` is a rule that applies to ALL of them — a
`Delete @ age 30` would take the prod->QA feed mirror and every cold candle
shard with it, silently, over the following 30 days.
So EVERY rule in this file MUST carry a `condition.matchesPrefix`, and every
prefix in it MUST start with one of the prefixes on the ALLOW-LIST that
setup-gcs-lifecycle.sh declares:
edgar/              MONEY-979   the SEC filing archive
feeds/TIINGO/ws/    MONEY-1309  raw websocket ticks
That is not a convention: setup-gcs-lifecycle.sh REFUSES to apply a policy
file with a rule outside the allow-list, and
packages/core/__tests__/ops/edgar-infra-coverage.test.ts +
packages/core/__tests__/ops/tiingo-realtime-infra.test.ts fail on one.
## THE SECOND LOCK: a Delete rule may never SHORTEN onto a shared root
The allow-list alone is not enough, because the allow-list is itself a line
in a file somebody can edit. `feeds/TIINGO/ws/` shortened to `feeds/` — one
deleted path segment, in a diff that looks like tidying — is a `Delete @ 30`
over the ENTIRE prod->QA feed mirror. Nothing errors; QA's replay starts
missing objects a month later and falls back to scraping NSE/BSE, which is a
SOFT failure by design and therefore says nothing.
So the applier ALSO carries a hard-coded PROTECTED_ROOTS list and refuses
any Delete rule whose prefix would sweep one of them — the test is `root
starts with prefix`, i.e. the prefix is the root or SHORTER, which catches
`feeds/`, `feeds`, `fe` and `` alike. `edgar/filings/` is on that list too,
which closes a hole the allow-list never covered: a rule with prefix
`edgar/` is perfectly allow-listed and would delete the permanent filing
archive.
## Why these three rules and no others
edgar/bulk/**      DELETED at 30 days. These are `companyfacts.zip`
(1,407,685,214 B) and `submissions.zip`
(1,560,992,008 B), re-fetched and superseded NIGHTLY.
Keeping every night's copy is ~90 GB a month of bytes
that were already parsed into Mongo and the cold shards.
30 days rather than 2 so a reparse of last month's
ledger is still possible without re-downloading 3 GB
from SEC on a shared 9 req/s budget.
edgar/filings/**   -> NEARLINE at 30 days. Permanent (this is the archive
the runbook reparses from when the numbers look wrong),
but read only on a reparse, so a class whose retrieval
costs more and whose storage costs less is the right
trade. NOT deleted, ever: deleting these would make a
mapping fix cost a full re-fetch of ~330 GB/yr of
filings from sec.gov.
databento/**       -> NEARLINE at 30 days, and NEVER deleted — MONEY-1373.
The raw vendor archive: the .csv.zst files each batch
job produced plus their manifest/metadata/condition
support files. Read only on a RE-LOAD (the loader is
found wrong, or a symbol-year has to be rebuilt), so
the Nearline trade is the same one edgar/filings/
takes: cheaper storage against a retrieval fee on a
read that almost never happens.
A Delete rule here would be the most expensive
possible mistake in this file. These bytes are the
only copy of data bought once inside a ONE-MONTH
Standard subscription that is cancelled afterwards, so
deleting them turns a re-load into a re-PURCHASE.
`databento/` is therefore on setup-gcs-lifecycle.sh's
PROTECTED_ROOTS as well as its ALLOW_PREFIXES — the
allow-list lets this rule exist, and the protected
root is what refuses a Delete written against the
same prefix later.
feeds/TIINGO/ws/** DELETED at 30 days — MONEY-1309. Raw websocket ticks,
written as JSONL under `feeds/TIINGO/ws/{date}/` by the
always-on `tiingo-realtime-{env}` service. Unlike every
other object under `feeds/`, these are NOT an input QA
replays and NOT an archive anything reparses: the bars
derived from them land in `candles`, which is a
REFERENCE_COLLECTION and reaches QA by mongorestore. The
raw stream is kept only long enough to re-derive a bad
day, and a full trading day of US ticks is orders of
magnitude larger than the bars it produces.
IT IS ALSO EXCLUDED FROM THE prod->QA MIRROR. That is a
SECOND file — scripts/ops/sync-prod-to-qa.sh passes
`--exclude` to `gcloud storage rsync` — and the two are
one rule written twice, which is this repo's most
reliable drift shape. tiingo-realtime-infra.test.ts pins
them to each other; do not edit this prefix without
reading that test's failure message.
`matchesStorageClass: ["STANDARD"]` on the transition is deliberate. Without
it the rule keeps matching objects that are ALREADY Nearline, and while GCS
will not bill a transition to the class an object is already in, a condition
that can never stop matching is one you cannot reason about when a third rule
arrives. It also makes the rule a no-op the moment somebody sets the bucket's
default class to NEARLINE.
NOT covered here, deliberately:
edgar/text/**    re-derivable from edgar/filings, but small; a rule would
trade a real reparse cost for a negligible saving.
edgar/facts/**   gz-JSONL cold shards, READ ON THE REQUEST PATH.
edgar/13f/**     the evicted-holdings shards, READ ON THE REQUEST PATH by
packages/core/src/us-fundamentals/cold-holdings.ts. A
Nearline transition here would put a retrieval charge on a
user-facing read.
feeds/** (rest)  the exchange-feed archive QA REPLAYS. Ageing any of it out
turns a replay hit into a replay MISS, which falls back to
scraping the exchange and reports nothing.
candles/**       the cold price shards, READ ON THE REQUEST PATH by
CandleRepository.
Age is measured from the object's CREATION time, and a GCS put REPLACES —
every shard writer here reads-merges-writes, so a rewritten object's clock
restarts. That is why neither shard prefix could be aged out safely even if
we wanted to: a hot manager's shard would survive and a quiet one would not.
The tick objects are the one prefix immune to that, because they are
APPEND-ONLY-BY-DATE: a given day's object is written once and never rewritten,
so its creation clock means exactly what the rule assumes it means.

rule._rule: edgar/bulk/** — superseded nightly, so 30 days is a reparse window, not retention.
databento/** — MONEY-1373 raw vendor archive. NEVER a Delete: these bytes are the only copy of data bought once, and deleting them turns a re-load into a re-purchase of a $199 Standard month.
feeds/TIINGO/ws/** — MONEY-1309 raw websocket ticks. Re-derivation window, not an archive. MUST stay this exact prefix: `feeds/` alone deletes the prod->QA mirror.
